issue:
  number: 3602
  repo: encode/httpx
  title: httpx.BaseTransport dropped from 0.28.1 to 1.0.dev1
  state: closed
  author: SoundDesignerToBe
  created: 1y ago
  type: none
  body: "Reproduce:

```shell
uv pip install -U --pre httpx
python
```

```python
import httpx
```
```python
httpx.BaseTransport
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<input>", line 1, in <module>
AttributeError: module 'httpx' has no attribute 'BaseTransport'. Did you mean: 'Transport'?
```

This happens after upgrading from the latest stable version to the published dev version"

cases.title: Pytest can't handle custom classes in parameterized tests (major bug).
cases.source_format: gh-axi full text; relative age strings are preserved as displayed, not converted into inferred dates.
cases.source_text:
issue:
  number: 14560
  repo: pytest-dev/pytest
  title: Pytest can't handle custom classes in parameterized tests (major bug).
  state: closed
  author: ketchupee1
  created: 5mo ago
  type: none
  body: "Hello.

I'm having an issue with Pytest where I'm unable to run parameterized tests with custom class objects. 

Script path: ...\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314\Lib\site-packages\_pytest\python.py
Lineno: 1052

Error:  
```
1052: in _idval_from_value
    elif isinstance(getattr(val, "\_\_name\_\_", None), str):
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
E   KeyError:  '\_\_name\_\_'
-------------------------------------
```

I should note that on my side, the test that now is unable to run had passed before about one week ago,  and nothing has changed within the test script itself. 

It seems to be that my custom class, which is basically a wrapper around the Python Dict builtin class, causes the error to now raise, whereas if I convert this to a normal python Dict, the tests passes again."
comments[11]{author,created,body}:
  ketchupee1,5mo ago,"Hey, I just thought of something that may help: The class that wasn't working with Pytest is one that overrides the internal __getattr__ and __setattr__ methods, so Pytest was properly trying to use these methods and running into an issue. Though, again, this wasn't happening before with the exact same tests, so it is a recent error. "
  RonnyPfannschmidt,5mo ago,"Nope its okay to fall appartement on fundamentally broken messes 

If getattr raises keyerror that's fundamentally wrong "
  RonnyPfannschmidt,5mo ago,we need a basic reproducer and the current suggestion is  - if you parameterize with broken objects - use explicit ids
  ketchupee1,5mo ago,"Ah, eh, I'm a bit confused but basically I had a class called "DotDict" that assigned setattr and getattr to getitem and setitem, respectively. This was the sole cause behind the issue, though again, it worked previously in the same tests."
  RonnyPfannschmidt,5mo ago,"If the class was used then no error should have happened 

If a instance is used the error is expected "
  ketchupee1,5mo ago,"This doesn't really makes sense, if the class itself works for something, the class instance should work for that same something since it's easy to derive the class from the instance. Also why would one not use an instance, most of the time, the whole point of making a class is to use instances of it. Plus the same tests worked without any modifications, so the problem must be on Pytest's end.

I actually made a work around where I simply changed the default getattr and setattr behaviour if the attribute in question wasn't already defined. I still used the same instance as before, and nothing else had changed."
  RonnyPfannschmidt,5mo ago,"Again this is expected python behavior and its a reasonable constraint for pytest not to handle broken user instances everywhere 


The class itself is not broken but a instance of it is in the case of having getattr raise keyerror

The way to use that in pytest is explicit ids "
  ketchupee1,5mo ago,"Thanks, but I don't actually know what an Id is, or at least not in this exact context, that is. I only mention it because that's what the error message said, but the handling of id's is not on my side of the field. In fact I shouldn't be managing id's, I don't plan to go digging through and modifying Pytest internals. "
  RonnyPfannschmidt,5mo ago,"`pytest.param(MyBroken(), id="broken")`"
  ketchupee1,5mo ago,"Yeah, no, I'm not responsible for that. At what point do you think I magically downloaded pytests inner workings into my brain to the point I know how to implement this id mararky?

And also, if it worked before and doesn't work after with no changes on my end, clearly it's not an issue on my end, because of the simple law of cause and effect."
  Pierre-Sassoulas,5mo ago,"It's very hard to understand what you're talking about because you didn't take the time to give a minimal reproducer for the problem. The tone also isn't great. Remember that open source code is a gift from volunteers. You don't have to like it, but nobody owes you a better gift. "
